text: Suddenly the scene changes. <break time="0.8s" /> And now he stands. <break time="0.8s" /> At the gate of his own home. <break time="0.8s" /> Which shines. <break time="0.8s" /> In the bright morning sunshine. <break time="0.8s" /> He must have traveled the whole night. <break time="0.8s" /> For everything is just as he left it. <break time="0.8s" /> Bright and beautiful and peaceful. <break time="0.8s" /> As he pushes open the gate. <break time="0.8s" /> And walks up the path. <break time="0.8s" /> He sees a flutter of white clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> Near the house. <break time="0.8s" /> His wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking fresh and sweet. <break time="0.8s" /> Steps down from the veranda. <break time="0.8s" /> And waits for him. <break time="0.8s" /> At the bottom of the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> She stands there smiling. <break time="0.8s" /> With a joy that cannot be put into words. <break time="0.8s" /> And he runs forward. <break time="0.8s" /> With his arms wide open. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as he is about to hold her. <break time="0.8s" /> He feels a stunning blow. <break time="0.8s" /> On the back of his neck. <break time="0.8s" /> A blinding white light. <break time="0.8s" /> Blazes all around him. <break time="0.8s" /> With a sound like a cannon. <break time="0.8s" /> And then all is darkness and silence. <break time="0.8s" /> Peyton Farquhar was dead. <break time="0.8s" /> His body swinging gently from side to side. <break time="0.8s" /> Beneath the timbers of the Owl Creek bridge.
